maya: Quick share — ran end-to-end embed + reranker throughput matrix across regions and hardware. pushing raw numbers and a short summary.

maya: TL;DR: GPU wins for high-dim embeddings and small-batch low-latency work, CPU is surprisingly competitive for large-batch offline jobs in eu-central due to node-local caching.

maya: Summary numbers (avg QPS for embed + rerank pipeline, 2048-dim vectors, 128 request batch -> internal batching + rerank 16):
  - us-west (A100 80GB): 14.2k qps, p99 latency 82ms
  - us-east (A10G): 9.1k qps, p99 130ms
  - eu-central (GPU pool mixed T4/A10): 7.5k qps, p99 180ms
  - eu-central (CPU 32core cached): 3.8k qps, p99 240ms (but sustained throughput for large batch jobs >12k qps when batching to 1024)

liam: nice. what about dims 768 / 1024? and batch scaling?

maya: 768-dim (batch 64): A100 ~18.6k qps, T4 ~11.3k, CPU ~2.1k. 1024-dim sits between 768 and 2048 as expected. throughput scales sublinearly after batch 256 on GPUs due to memory/KV-cache pressure.

sophia: any kernel differences? flash-attn / fused vs cuBLAS paths?

maya: yes — switching from cuBLAS matmul->custom kernel (flash-attn fused) gave ~18% latency reduction for 2048-dim on A100. On T4 the gains are smaller (~6%) and sometimes unstable at very long sequences.

maya: commands we used for reproducibility:
```
python bench_pipeline.py \
  --model reranker-v2 \
  --emb-dim 2048 \
  --batch 128 \
  --rerank-k 16 \
  --device cuda \
  --kernel flash_attn \
  --quant none \
  --warmup 200 \
  --steps 2000
```

esther: did you try int8/quantized kernels for embeddings? curious about throughput vs quality.

maya: yup — ran PerChannel int8 with symmetric calibration. Performance: A100 + int8 -> +40% qps (2048-dim, batch 128 went from 14.2k to 19.9k), latency p99 dropped ~25ms. BUT quality: MRR on our eval set dropped ~0.9 points absolute for reranker scores after naive int8.

sophia: can calibration/per-channel fix that?

maya: partially. per-channel + activation clipping + small re-calibration dataset brought regression down to ~0.2 MRR points while retaining +30% throughput. So recommend staged rollout and eval flags.

liam: any regional network effects? EU vs US numbers seemed off.

maya: eu-central GPU pool had lower per-GPU throughput because of older kernel builds on the node image (missing fused kernel and older CUDA 11.4). Upgrading node image -> aligned with A10G numbers in us-east. Also notice CPU cached path in eu had great large-batch perf because data was local and avoided cross-AZ egress.

infra-bot: perf-run: 1759123468 finished (artifact: <https://internal.redwood/charts/bench/1759123468>).

liam: ok action items:
  - infra: schedule node-image rollout with flash-attn kernels to eu-central (esther)
  - ml-eng: run canary with int8 per-channel on reranker traffic (maya + sophia), include eval set and log MRR and top1 precision
  - bench: add 2 configs to nightly matrix: batch sizes [32,128,512,1024], dims [768,1024,2048], kernels [cuBLAS, flash_attn, fused_fast]

esther: noted. will queue image rollout and add telemetry to ensure we can revert quickly.

sophia: i'll add the eval harness and cal set. also propose a small A/B that gates int8 only for low-risk routes (non-critical search) first.

maya: final note: for capacity sizing — use GPU for sub-200ms p99 SLOs and dims >=1024, CPU can be a cost-effective fallback for high-throughput offline embedding generation with large batch sizes. We'll include these in the onboarding doc for new models.

liam: solid. thanks for the run and artifact link. :thumbsup:
